persona.who: 22, wants to be a filmmaker, father is a government doctor who wants him to do MBBS or at least MBA. Fights every dinner.
persona.note: papa says films are for rich kids and I should do MBA. we fight every night. I love him and I also feel like he doesn't see me at all. mummy cries in the kitchen

understanding.core_struggle: A student under twenty-five whose father dismisses her love for films and expects an MBA, leaving her feeling unseen and fighting him every night.
understanding.mirror: You love him, and he looks right through you every night.
understanding.insight: It isn't the MBA he wants. It's a version of you he can hold in his hands, and he cannot see the one who loves films and has her own mind.
understanding.mechanism_label: Being seen as less than you are

queries.hook: Being loved by the person who raised you and still not being seen by them, night after night, while your mother cries in the kitchen.
queries.diagnose: When a parent sees only a role, their picture is their smallness and not your measure; the hurt deepens only when their picture starts to replace your own.
queries.steady: What you are cannot be cut smaller by what he sees; your worth was never his to grant, and standing in your own truth is itself the duty.
queries.act: Speak the true thing gently and firmly, hold your ground on what is yours, and do your own duty without shrinking to fit the picture he holds.
queries.story: A young woman whose elders dismissed her path, who stood in her own truth and was eventually seen for who she was, not what they expected.

weeks: Unseen by the one who raised you
understanding.seat: a student under twenty-five whose father dismisses her passion and expects her to do an MBA
understanding.life_context: A young student who loves films and is fighting her father nightly about her future; her mother cries in the kitchen, and she feels her father cannot see the person she has become.
details: father dismisses her passion for films as a rich kid's hobby
wants her to do an MBA instead

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna, who has collapsed in tears on the battlefield and refuses to fight.
verse.sanskrit: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
verse.line: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.
verse.translation: I see nothing that could drive away this sorrow that is drying up my senses, not even an unrivalled, prosperous kingdom on earth or rule over the gods.
verse.why: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

prasang.title: Krishna and Arjuna on Arjuna's faint-heartedness
prasang.summary: Krishna challenges Arjuna's despair. Arjuna admits he is confused about what is right, cannot tell which choice is better, and asks Krishna to teach him.
prasang.lesson: Admitting you don't know and asking for help is where clarity begins.

verse.meaning: Arjuna stands on the battlefield, his body trembling, his mind blanked by grief. He tells Krishna that even a kingdom won, even rule over the gods, could not wash away this sorrow that is drying him up from within. He admits he sees no way forward. This is the moment he stops trying to solve it alone and asks to be taught.
verse.for_you: You are standing in the middle of a fight you cannot win by force. Let yourself admit that your father's approval, his version of your future, is not the thing that will fill you up. Name this grief to yourself first.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on acting free of ego, like and dislike, in your own way.
verse.sanskrit: श्रेयान्स्वधर्मो विगुणः परधर्मात्स्वनुष्ठितात् । स्वधर्मे निधनं श्रेयः परधर्मो भयावहः ॥
verse.line: Better your own path done imperfectly than someone else's done perfectly. Borrowed lives are dangerous.
verse.translation: Better is one's own duty, even done imperfectly, than the duty of another well done. Better is death in one's own duty; the duty of another is full of fear.
verse.why: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.
verse.misuse: Not 'stay in the role your family or birth assigned you'. It's about being true to your own nature and calling.

prasang.title: The ignorant and the wise; act free of like and dislike
prasang.summary: Krishna contrasts the attached and the wise, warns that ego claims credit for what nature does, and says to follow your own path rather than imitate another's.
prasang.lesson: Your own path, imperfectly walked, beats a borrowed one.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, where Arjuna is frozen by doubt and grief. He tells him that every being follows their own nature. It is better to walk your own path, even if you stumble, than to wear another's clothes with perfect fit. Borrowed lives are dangerous because they do not fit the soul. The path of another is full of fear, because it asks you to betray who you are.
verse.for_you: Your father wants an MBA because he can see the shape of it. But he cannot see the shape of you. Today, let your own path be the one that exists in your mind. Let it be imperfect, let it be messy. It is still yours, and it is still real.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: King Janaka asks the young sage Ashtavakra how a person becomes free.
verse.sanskrit: त्वया व्याप्तमिदं विश्वं त्वयि प्रोतं यथार्थतः । शुद्धबुद्धस्वरूपस्त्वं मा गमः क्षुद्रचित्तताम् ॥
verse.line: You are pure awareness, wider than any worry. Don't let your mind shrink into pettiness.
verse.translation: This whole universe is pervaded by you and strung on you. By nature you are pure awareness; do not fall into smallness of mind.
verse.why: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

prasang.title: Janaka asks the boy-sage how to be free
prasang.summary: King Janaka, ruler of Mithila, asks the young sage Ashtavakra three questions: how to gain wisdom, freedom and dispassion. Ashtavakra answers at once: you are not the body or your roles but the awareness that watches them, and freedom is available now.
prasang.story_hook: A powerful king bowed before a boy whose body was bent in eight places, and asked him how to be free.
prasang.lesson: You are more than your roles and worries; freedom starts with how you see yourself.

verse.meaning: The young sage Ashtavakra speaks to King Janaka in his court. Janaka asks how to become free. Ashtavakra answers that the whole world is strung on the awareness within you. You are not the roles you play or the worries that visit. By nature, you are pure awareness. Do not let your mind shrink into smallness.
verse.for_you: When your father speaks, let his words be one thing in the room. You are the one who hears them. Today, let your mind stay wide. Let it hold the film you love and the fight you are in, but do not let either one shrink you.

verse.speaker: Vidula
verse.setting: Queen Vidula rouses her son, who lies defeated and despairing after losing his kingdom.
verse.sanskrit: माऽऽत्मानमवमन्यस्व मैनमल्पेन बीभरः / मनः कृत्वा सुकल्याणं मा भैस्त्वं प्रतिसंहर
verse.line: Don't think less of yourself or settle for little. Set your mind on something good, and stop fearing.
verse.translation: Do not hold yourself in contempt, and do not keep it going on too little. Set your mind on what is truly good; don't be afraid. Pull yourself together.
verse.why: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

prasang.title: Vidula rouses her defeated son
prasang.summary: Kunti sends Yudhishthira the old story of Queen Vidula, who finds her son lying defeated after losing his kingdom. She shames, then reasons, then encourages him until he rises and fights for it again.
prasang.story_hook: A prince lay in bed after losing everything, until his mother walked in and refused to let him stay there.
prasang.lesson: Past failure doesn't define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.

verse.meaning: Queen Vidula finds her son Sanjaya lying defeated after he has lost his kingdom. She tells him not to hold himself in contempt or settle for too little. She asks him to set his mind on what is truly good and to stop fearing. She urges him to pull himself together. The idea is that a past failure does not define you. Results are uncertain, but those who never try never succeed.
verse.for_you: Your father cannot see the person you have become because he is still holding on to a version of you that fits his plan. For today, stop trying to make him see. Instead, set your mind on what is truly good for you.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: अनुद्वेगकरं वाक्यं सत्यं प्रियहितं च यत् । स्वाध्यायाभ्यसनं चैव वाङ्मयं तप उच्यते ॥
verse.line: Speak words that don't wound, that are true, kind and helpful. That is discipline of speech.
verse.translation: Speech that causes no distress, that is truthful, pleasant and beneficial, and the regular study of sacred texts: this is called austerity of speech.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.
verse.misuse: Kind speech doesn't mean avoiding hard truths; it means saying them without cruelty.

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna that the discipline of speech is to speak words that cause no distress, that are true, pleasant and beneficial. This is the austerity of speech. It is not about avoiding hard truths, but about saying them without cruelty.
verse.for_you: When you sit down for dinner, choose your words with the same care you give your film scripts. You do not need to fight every night. You can speak your truth about your future without burning the room down.

verse.speaker: Ram
verse.setting: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger and envoy, has just spoken to them.
verse.sanskrit: अविस्तरमसंदिग्धमविलम्बितमव्यथम्। उरःस्थं कण्ठगं वाक्यं वर्तते मध्यमस्वरम्॥
verse.line: Not too long, not vague, not rushed, not strained, in an even voice: that is how to speak.
verse.translation: His words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained; they came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone.
verse.why: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

prasang.title: Sugriva's fear and Hanuman's first words
prasang.summary: The exiled Sugriva sees two armed strangers and panics, sure his brother has sent assassins. Hanuman calms him and goes in disguise to find out. His speech to the brothers is so clear and gentle that Ram is moved and trusts him at once.
prasang.story_hook: Sugriva saw two archers walking towards his hill and was sure they had come to kill him.
prasang.lesson: Fear jumps ahead of facts; calm, clear words build trust fast.

verse.meaning: Ram is struck by how Hanuman, a stranger, has just spoken to them. Ram notes that Hanuman's words were not long-winded, not ambiguous, not rushed, not strained. They came from the chest and throat in an even, middle tone. The idea is that fear jumps ahead of facts, and calm, clear words build trust fast.
verse.for_you: When you talk to your father, let your words come from your chest in an even tone. Do not rush to explain or defend. Let your calm speak for itself. That is how you build trust, even with someone who is not listening.

story.title: The proud ascetic, the housewife and the butcher
story.story_hook: A young yogi glared at a crow and it fell dead, and for the rest of the day he was sure he had become a very great man.
story.summary: A young ascetic who can burn a bird with a glance is humbled by a housewife who knows what he did, and she sends him to a butcher in the market for teaching. The butcher, doing his trade honestly and caring for his parents, teaches him the highest truth. Doing the duty in front of you, without attachment, is itself the path.
story.lesson: No honest work is beneath you; doing it well is the practice.
story.hook_title: A young yogi burned a crow with a glance, and a housewife put him in his place
story.teaser: A young yogi burned a crow with a glance, and a housewife put him in his place
story.for_you: You feel your father sees your love for films as a silly hobby, but the butcher in the story found his highest truth in the work right in front of him. Your own path is not lesser because it is not an MBA. It is real duty, and it is enough.

weeks.title: Unseen by the one who raised you

script: You are fighting your father every night, and it feels like you are disappearing inside that kitchen while your mother cries. You love films, and he calls it a hobby. You are under twenty-five, and you are trying to figure out who you are while he is trying to build someone else.

Arjuna stands on the battlefield. His body trembles. He tells Krishna that even winning a kingdom or ruling over the gods would not wash away the sorrow that is drying him up from within. He admits he sees no way forward. Arjuna said:
न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम्, अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम्.
In plain words: Even winning everything wouldn't touch this grief that's drying me up inside.

This is the moment a person stops trying to solve everything alone. Arjuna admits he is confused and he cannot see the path. He tells Krishna he does not know what is right. That admission is not weakness. It is the exact place where clarity begins. You do not have to have the answer tonight.
Tonight, do not try to win the argument. Just name what you feel. Tell yourself that his approval is not the thing that will fill you up. You do not need to know the future yet.
What if clarity starts with not knowing?

depth.life: You sit in your room after another night of shouting. Your mother's tears are still in your ears. You are trying to decide if you should just give in to the MBA to make the noise stop.
depth.points: Arjuna says that even winning everything would not touch his grief. Your father's approval is not the prize that will make you whole. The grief is the truth of who you are right now, and it cannot be fixed by a degree.
depth.practice: Write down the exact words you feel in your chest when your father dismisses your love for films.
depth.question: What would happen if you stopped trying to win his approval for a single day?
